acceptedAnswer.text: Amazon Ads management is the work of running sponsored ads on Amazon and improving the listings and brand content they lead to, so that ad spend turns into profitable sales.

mainEntity.name: How does Amazon Ads work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We start with the listing, then structure sponsored ads around your stock and margins, and review the account every week. We read results next to total sales, because Amazon attributes only some sales to ads.

Your ad spend is paid to Amazon and sits outside our fee. We quote our fee after a call, once we have seen the account and agreed what we will run. We do not publish a price list, because the right scope depends on your spend and your margins.
No. We cannot guarantee sales or a ROAS. We commit to a clear structure, careful stock planning and honest reporting, with results judged on contribution margin, not on what a platform reports.

Amazon is mainly a D2C and product channel, so this page leads with D2C brands. It also applies to B2B and education brands: the same method, measured on qualified leads, enquiries and admissions instead of orders. For B2B and education, lead generation is usually the better fit.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: Seller or vendor account access, your product catalogue and margins, current stock levels and a view of your restock plan.

hub.sub: Sponsored ads, listings and brand content planned together, around your stock, and read against total sales rather than ad-attributed sales alone.

leaks.note: Screens are illustrative recreations of each platform's interface, not client data. Platform names and logos belong to their owners.
leaks.lede: On Amazon the ad, the listing and the stock work as one system. Each stage below is where it breaks, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Advertising a listing that does not convert.
stages.why: Ads send shoppers to your listing. A weak title, images or price wastes every click.
stages.does: We improve titles, bullet points, images and rich content, so the traffic you pay for has a reason to buy.

stages.breaks: One campaign with every keyword mixed together.
stages.why: Mixed campaigns hide which keywords earn and which drain budget.
stages.does: We separate campaigns by purpose (defending brand terms, finding new ones, targeting products) and set a budget for each.

stages.breaks: Running ads on products that are low or out of stock.
stages.why: Advertising stock you cannot fulfil wastes spend and can harm rankings and the customer's trust.
stages.does: We plan ads around inventory, and pause or shift spend when availability changes.

stages.breaks: A bare listing with nothing to build trust.
stages.why: Shoppers compare on Amazon. A clear brand store and rich content signal a brand worth buying.
stages.does: We build brand stores and rich content that present the range clearly and support the ads.

stages.breaks: Judging Amazon Ads on ad-attributed sales alone.
stages.why: Ads also lift sales that Amazon does not attribute to them. Reading only attributed sales misjudges what the ads do.
stages.does: We read ad performance alongside total sales and your margin, so budgets follow what actually adds profit.

good.t: You sell physical products on Amazon and want ads and listings run together.
good.why: Amazon is mainly a product channel, so it suits D2C brands that can keep stock and want spend read against total sales.

not.t: You want ads to fix a weak product, a thin margin or a stock problem.
not.why: Ads amplify what the listing and the stock already are, so those need to be sound first.
